title: 报告：13TB Steam 数据泄露，源于用户访问“可公开访问端点”

Report: 13TB of Steam data from 2003-2013 leaked to public
PC
Business
News
Report: 13TB of Steam data leaked after users access 'publicly accessible endpoint'
The leaked data apparently includes beta builds and screenshots of pre-release Valve titles—and games from other publishers like EA and WB Games.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
August 31, 2026
2 Min Read
Image by Rokas via Adobe Stock
Steam platform owner and
Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
developer Valve appears to have suffered an unusual breach sometime last week. As reported by
Kotaku
, the leak—dubbed "the Steam2 leak" by
users on X
—contained 13TB of data contained on Steam uploaded between the years 2003 and 2013.
"Steam2" here appears to refer to the old name of Steam's server infrastructure, (per
Ars Technica
)which was upgraded to the modern SteamPipes system in 2013. This data apparently includes early versions and screenshots of games produced by Valve (such as
Left 4 Dead 2
,
Portal 2
, and the never-released
Half-Life 2: Episode 3
).
But this leak doesn't just concern Valve's games. Beta builds of high-profile titles like BioWare and EA's
Dragon Age: Origins
and Rocksteady and WB Games'
Batman: Arkham Asylum
were reportedly discovered in the dump.
X user "Gabe Follower" shared screenshots of the leaked data on the platform, and claimed that they verified that there was "no hacking" involved in obtaining the information. The data was reportedly visible after accessing a "publicly accessable [sic] endpoint." It's unclear what
endpoint
this individual was referring to. Sources speaking to Ars Technica explained that the leak may not have taken place at Valve's end, but rather may be a breach of third-party servers that hosted data gathered during previous leaks.
Related:
Steam adds wishlist categories and cross-region gifting
The contents of such a leak do make for an informative historical look at the early development of Valve's highly-celebrated games, but also raise security questions for other companies whose data was exposed. It's unclear at this time how much sensitive data from third-party publishers was included in the leak, or what the ramifications might be of said data being available to the public.
Game Developer has reached out to Valve for comment on this leak and will update this story when teh company responds
.
